title: Major outcomes in moderately hypercholesterolemic, hypertensive patients randomized to pravastatin vs usual care: The Antihypertensive and Lipid-Lowering Treatment to Prevent Heart Attack Trial (ALLHAT-LLT)
authors: ALLHAT Officers and Coordinators for the ALLHAT Collaborative Research Group
followUp: mean 4.8 years; mortality reported at 6 years
population: Ambulatory adults aged 55 years or older with hypertension, at least one other coronary risk factor, LDL cholesterol 120 to 189 mg/dL (100 to 129 mg/dL with known coronary heart disease) and triglycerides below 350 mg/dL, at 513 North American centres; mean age 66 years, 14% with coronary heart disease, 35% with type 2 diabetes
funder: The funding statement of the JAMA report could not be read: the publisher page returns HTTP 403. PubMed records contract N01-HC-35130 from the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute. An ALLHAT publication in the Journal of the American Heart Association states: the ALLHAT study was supported by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NO1-HC-35130); ALLHAT investigators received contributions of study medications supplied by Pfizer (amlodipine and doxazosin), AstraZeneca (atenolol and lisinopril), and Bristol-Myers Squibb (pravastatin) and financial support provided by Pfizer. Whether Pfizer had any role in design, analysis or publication is not stated in a readable source.
result: Results read from the abstract. Non-blinded pravastatin 40 mg/day (n = 5170) against usual care (n = 5185). During the trial 32% of usual-care participants with and 29% without coronary heart disease started lipid-lowering drugs. At year 4 total cholesterol was reduced by 17% with pravastatin and 8% with usual care, and LDL cholesterol (random sample) by 28% and 11%. All-cause mortality relative risk 0.99 (95% CI 0.89 to 1.11; P = 0.88), with 6-year mortality 14.9% against 15.3%. Coronary heart disease events relative risk 0.91 (0.79 to 1.04; P = 0.16), with 6-year rates 9.3% against 10.4%.
